preamble: In the Baxter–Sagart reconstruction, Old Chinese voiceless nasals *m̥ˤ- (filed here under m, as the atlas has no separate voiceless-nasal symbol) became the Middle Chinese velar fricative x- (xw- before round vowels), later h- in Mandarin and f- before round vowels in Cantonese and Hakka. The OC voiceless nasal rests on reconstruction (from phonetic-series contacts between x- and m- words such as 黑 and 墨), not on directly attested forms.
sources: Baxter, W. H., & Sagart, L. (2014). Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction. Oxford University Press. https://doi.org/10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199945375.001.0001
